title: Michele Tafoya: from unassuming NFL sideline reporter to rightwing firebrand | NFL | The Guardian
description: The former Sunday Night Football stalwart is now one step from a seat in the US Senate. And she could cause a shock in liberal Minnesota
Author: Andrew Lawrence
Headline: The former Sunday Night Football stalwart is now one step from a seat in the US Senate. And she could cause a shock in liberal Minnesota
Content: Michele Tafoya emerged victorious from Minnesota’s Republican primary.Photograph: Star Tribune/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMichele Tafoya emerged victorious from Minnesota’s Republican primary.Photograph: Star Tribune/Getty ImagesNFLMichele Tafoya: from unassuming NFL sideline reporter to rightwing firebrandThe former Sunday Night Football stalwart is now one step from a seat in the US Senate. And she could cause a shock in liberal MinnesotaAndrew LawrenceThu 20 Aug 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 05.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAs the third leg of NBC’s Sunday Night Football crew alongside play-by-play man Al Michaels and the tart-tongued analyst Cris Collinsworth, Michele Tafoya was a paragon of deference and neutrality for 11 years as an NFL sideline reporter, dutifully relating boilerplate tactics, talking points and injury updates when she wasn’t nodding along to softball interviews or fumbling throughhammy production gimmicksfor viewers who might have been too offline to get the bit. She was almost pathologically committed to not doing anything to draw attention to herself or her gender in an era when sideline reporting was a fast track to national celebrity. Even her football takes hewed to the middle. (“New Orleans doesn’t want to lose to Atlantatwice in a season…”) Anyone who says they saw the 61-year-old emerging as a rightwing firebrand was watching a different game.And yet here we are. Last week, Tafoya was the decisive winner ofMinnesota’s US Senate Republican primary, earning the party’s nomination for November’s general election. Even more striking: she beat back eight challengers, not least Adam Schwarze, the party-endorsed pro-gun, pro-military ex-Navy SEAL, and Royce White, theanti-leftist, anti-trans NBA flameout currentlytesting WNBA gender norms.Next, Tafoya will face off against Minnesota lieutenant governor Peggy Flanagan – a Native American trailblazer, progressive champion and convenient stand-in for governor Tim Walz, Tafoya’s favorite political punching bag. (She’s been going after Walz since Kamala Harris tapped him for the 2024 Democratic presidential ticket, alleging wanton corruption.) And even though Schwarze has so farrefused to back Tafoya, Minnesota Republicans are starting to like their chances with her in the race, particularly as her fundraising surge gives her the resources to compete with Flanagan. Recent polling gives the lieutenant governor aseven-point leadover Tafoya, a healthy advantage but by no means insurmountable.With her midwest mom vibes and broadcast polish, Tafoya presents as a conservative correction to Maga that may play well in a state that hasn’t sent a Republican senator to Washington in 24 years. But the difference is mostly packaging. On the issues that define today’s Republican Party – cops, immigration and the culture wars – Tafoya is every bit as committed as the chorus. In a recent Fox News appearance, she claimed there is a sense of fatigue among Minnesotans around progressive causes. “Minnesotans are exhausted,”saidTafoya, a Southern California transplant who put down roots in the 1990s. “I have talked to hundreds of voters in Minnesota who have told me, ‘Gosh, I went on vacation this summer. I didn’t want to tell people where I was from because it’s embarrassing.’ And it’s true.”It was a curious read on a famously left-leaning electorate, especially for an Emmy-winning reporter. But Tafoya gets away with it because her bland TV reputation trained audiences to hear her as harmless. So the bombshells don’t always register on arrival; especially to people who already agree with her, they sound less like provocations than conversation, another injury update perhaps.That’s not accidental. As her time on SNF was winding down in 2021, Tafoya appeared as a guest host on The View, an audition for the conservative seat on the panel that had been opened after Meghan McCain’s departure. On her first day, Tafoya sparred with Joy Behar over vaccinations, saying “the flu kills people too” in response to mounting Covid fatalities; she pushed back when Whoopi Goldberg suggested white people need to take more accountability for institutional racism. “[White people have] been doing that since the Civil War,” Tafoyasaid. “I’m not saying they’re perfect.”On day two, Tafoya bickered with Sunny Hostin about Colin Kaepernick, arguing the Pro Bowl quarterback turned social justice activist had been cut loose from theNFLbecause he couldn’t hack it any more. “I think all of us can agree that there is probably a lot to this story we still don’t know,” Tafoya, ostensibly an insider, said to audience jeers. “Oh, you’re going to groan at me?” she shot back. There was no day three.After that, Tafoya beat a hasty retreat to cable TV news, podcasting and social media, letting fly with some bracingly barbed takes – by her standards, at least. “This whole thing is insanity,” she said in a2024 OutKick riffon trans athletes. “Thank God for voices like JK Rowling and Riley Gaines and others. I don’t care if the male is intact or was born a male – they don’t belong in a women’s locker room, they don’t belong on a women’s team.” In a recent OutKick appearance, Tafoya called the WNBA veteran turned Maga pick-me Sophie Cunningham “a hero” for opposing a supposed trans-athlete encroachment that is – checks notes – almost entirely theoretical.View image in fullscreenMichele Tafoya was a familiar sight on NFL sidelines for years.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty ImagesCritically, she has positioned herself as a grounded Maga alternative. In 2022, she published an open letter urging Donald Trump not to seek reelection, bemoaning his “messy” politics – but has since come around to toe the party line. “I had my own little Trump protest,” shesaidin a 2025 Fox News appearance. “I didn’t think he should run again because I thought we needed a more conventional kind of candidate. Clearly, I was wrong.”On her campaign site, she is less extreme on some subjects than Maga Republicans, making a case for abortion access inthe first 12 weeks, connecting her position to her personal struggles to become a mother of two children. “I believe my position – aligned with Trump, respectful of the Dobbs decision, and firmly opposed to taxpayer funding – helps broaden the coalition of support, particularly with independents and others who seek middle ground,” she writes. “It reflects both principle and pragmatism as well as the political reality of this issue.”The day after Tafoya’s broadcast signoff from Super Bowl LVI, she was named co-chair of the 2022 Minnesota gubernatorial campaign mounted by Kendall Qualls, a Black ex-Army vet who shills a sadly familiar strain ofraceless conservative politics. After failing to receive the party endorsement, Qualls withdrew from the race three months before the primary.But Walz’s resounding reelection victory as Minnesota governor, vice-presidential nomination anda rightwing-driven scandal cyclethat has helped undo his progressive record, culminating in his retreat from elected office, would prove enough for Tafoya to hang a villainous origin story on, recasting herself as the lone figure who can fix what the left has broken. In another timeline, one could easily see her rushing through a soft-focus aside onWalz’s early football coaching careerbefore swiftly tossing it back to Al and Cris.That Tafoya became the first Sunday Night Football personality to jump into politics is undoubtedly the biggest twist in America’s most-watched television showsince Odell Beckham Jr’s one-handed grab. If anyone was going to be the GOP’s best chance of flipping a Senate seat in decidedly blue Minnesota, it was Tony Dungy –the Focus on the Family-coded, history-making Super Bowl coach who was a pioneering quarterback at the University of Minnesota and a visionary defensive coordinator with the Vikings.Tafoya has negotiated a political landscape that has been tough for sports candidates recently. The past four years alone have seen White (the WNBA troll), Herschel Walker (the Heisman Trophy winner), Steve Garvey (the decorated first baseman), Colin Allred (the ex-NFL linebacker) and Derek Dooley (the journeyman football coach) fail in their election bids. Only Walker landed softly, as Trump’s handpicked US ambassador to the Bahamas.Tommy Tuberville’sshambolic termas Alabama’s US senator has only served to underscore the fact that sporting greatness doesn’t necessarily translate to political skill. For all its talk of the collective, high-level athletics remains, at its core, a fundamentally individualistic endeavor pursued by inveterate glory hounds. It’s just their good fortune that the electorate takes to sports like catnip. The polls have Tuberville up 10 points in his Alabama governor bid. Once an Auburn fan,always an Auburn fan, after all.That’s what makes Tafoya’s candidacy so compelling: her long sports career placed her firmly in the spotlight, and yet she always understood her place on the sideline and deflected the attention anytime it lingered too long. She was there to illuminate, to facilitate and then quickly step out of the way so viewers could enjoy the game. That’s a formidable reservoir of residual trust to carry into politics. But will it still hold sway with Minnesota’s general election voters?No state rejects the Trumpian agenda as forcefully as the Land of 10,000 Lakes – hub of thecorporate DEI rollback backlash, bulwark against theICE incursion, laboratory ofpopulist governance. But Tafoya’s name recognition certainly gives her a fighting chance with an electorate that, for all its stolid pretensions, has a surprising record of falling hard forcelebritycandidates. Early in her broadcast career, Tafoya went by “Mickey Conley” because her radio co-host found her paternal surname too “ethnic” and not catchy enough. (Conley comes from her Irish-American mother’s side.) It’s the kind of assimilation story that could resonate in an immigration-friendly state if she didn’t also staunchly oppose federal amnesty programs. If she wins in November, Tafoya would become the first Latina Republican ever elected to the US Senate.Ultimately, though, what could hold Tafoya back is the very thing that once made her distinctive – being the standout woman in a man’s game. Maga world tends to prefer its telegenic female surrogates in front of the camera, as adornments to the movement rather than viable leaders – lest the tradwives start getting ideas. You could see how that impulse may be even stronger as Marjorie Taylor Greene, Nancy Mace and Lauren Boebert – all once fiercely loyal to Trump –broke ranks with himover the handling of the Epstein files.But in finally making herself the story, Tafoya has shown that slightly less extreme conservatism can be made more palatable through the veneer of fastidiously rehearsed professionalism. And if she pulls off an upset? Well, that’ll write the new rightwing political playbook.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sports mediaUS sportsUS politicsRepublicansMinnesotafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: ‘Why would you want to retire me?’: Novak Djokovic is still driven by doubt | Novak Djokovic | The Guardian
description: A revealing Prime Video documentary out Thursday explores the stubbornness, childhood scars and siege mentality still driving Novak Djokovic at 39
Author: Richard Deitsch
Headline: A revealing Prime Video documentary out Thursday explores the stubbornness, childhood scars and siege mentality still driving Novak Djokovic at 39
Content: Novak Djokovic celebrates a point at Wimbledon in June.Photograph: Matthew Stockman/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenNovak Djokovic celebrates a point at Wimbledon in June.Photograph: Matthew Stockman/Getty ImagesNovak Djokovic‘Why would you want to retire me?’: Novak Djokovic is still driven by doubtA revealing Prime Video documentary out Thursday explores the stubbornness, childhood scars and siege mentality still driving Novak Djokovic at 39Richard DeitschThu 20 Aug 2026 09.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe moment comes roughly 20 minutes into the thoughtfully done Prime Video documentary, Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter,where Djokovic, winner of 24 grand slam titles and owner of the most-ever total weeks atop the ATP rankings (428), gets to the core of what has driven him to tennis royalty.Djokovic can rightfully claim the title of the greatest male tennis player who has ever lived (“It is as clear as it gets – he is the best of all time,” Andre Agassi says in the doc) but how tennis fans feel about him has always been more complex than the universal love adorned on contemporaries Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal.“There is a word in Serbian calledinat,” Djokovic explains to the audience. “When people doubt you, when everyone is basically against you, that’s when you use thatinat,that force of stubbornness to prove everybody wrong. Thatinatis actually quite widespread in the mentality of Serbian people.”Djokovic’s medical malaise in Cincinnati exposes fraying edges of ageing great’s gameRead moreInatwould have been a worthy name for this 92-minute revealing exploration of Djokovic from director Jason Hehir, who has chronicled athletic giants including Michael Jordan in the Netflix/ESPN hitThe Last Danceand a literal giant (HBO’s André The Giant). Hehir said that a Djokovic documentary project had been in the works since 2017, though it was first brought to him in 2023 when Sadoux Kim, one of the executive producers, took him out to lunch and explained that a film exploration of Djokovic had endured stops and starts for years. Hehir officially took on the project the following year. It debuted Thursday.“I didn’t have specific interest in Novak as a tennis player but I knew that he had a reputation as an outspoken, often polarizing figure, and the more research I did the it felt like a great opportunity to profile a complex and compelling character,” Hehir said. “What put it over the top was the opportunity to follow a GOAT in real time.”Hehir said he was interested in telling a story that examined Djokovic at this specific point of his career and the challenges he faced navigating a young family with the selfishness it takes to remain a champion tennis player. (Much of this story will be familiar to hardcore tennis fans; Hehir said the film was made with a global audience in mind and what is revealing is the exploration into Djokovic’s mindset rather than his biography.)Djokovic’s wife, Jelena, offers the best psychological assessment of what drives her husband, a melange of genius, anger, playfulness and unexpressed emotions that date to his childhood in wartorn Serbia. At one point in the doc, Djokovic recalled tripping on the street in the dead of night as a young boy, unable to get the attention of his family who were running to safety, during the 1999 Nato bombings of Belgrade. Jelena describes tennis as a safe nest for her husband. “That’s the place where he finds love,” she says.View image in fullscreenNovak Djokovic (left) and Jason Hehir speak onstage during the Novak Djokovic: The Wolf In Winter world premiere at MoMA last month in New York.Photograph: Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for Prime VideoThe documentary does not shy away from Djokovic’sdeportation from Australiain 2022 prior to the Australian Open when the Australian government revoked his visa on the grounds that a recent Covid diagnosis did not justify an exemption to Australia’s requirement for visitors to be vaccinated.“I never said I’m against vaccine or pro-vaccine,” Djovikic says in the doc. “The anti-vax movement claimed that I’m their hero. I’ve never associated myself with any anti-vax, pro-vax or anything. I’m pro freedom to choose what you are going to do with the integrity of your body. I missed slams and tournaments. I didn’t play in America for a couple of years because I was not vaccinated. That’s fine. But in Australia, I was allowed. I’m not the scientist, I’m not the one who is setting the rules. I’m not the one that should debate that. I stood up for what I believe in. I stand for protection of my integrity and what I think is best for my body, and that’s it.”Djovovic is the greatest mover in the history of tennis but he cannot outrun the greatest impediment ahead of him – his age. He competed last week at the Cincinnati Open, his first tournament since Wimbledon, andwas bounced in his opening matchby Thiago Agustín Tirante of Argentina, the world No 50. Still, Djokovic has reached the semi-finals or better in six of his last seven grand slam tournaments and is ranked world No 5. Last month at Wimbledon he outlasted Felix Auger-Aliassime in a five-set, five-hour quarter-final epic before he was beaten by the eventual winner, Jannik Sinner. It is clear he can gear up for the big tournaments; the week-to-week stuff is much more difficult.“I know a lot of people are retiring me already, for many years,” Djokovic says in the film. “Why would you want to retire me when I am still playing and competing at the highest level? I’m still top 5, top 10 in the world. Why would I talk about retirement when I am proving to myself that I can still win?”Hehir said Djokovic initially did not want any mention of retirement in the documentary because he was understandably sick of addressing the subject. But the film-maker pushed Djokovic to see such questions as a compliment.“I told Novak, “We have to address this but it’s a compliment because people are fascinated by how long you can continue to do this,’” Hehir said. “The irony here is that I think that his career is going to be elongated because of the skepticism surrounding his retirement. That’s one of the things that drives him now. I’m sure with the result in Cincinnati there will be people asking, ‘Is this the beginning of the end?’ Well, they’ve been asking this about Novak for five years. I wouldn’t be surprised at all if he made a deep run at the US Open in a few weeks.”Explore more on these topicsNovak DjokovicTennisDocumentaryDocumentary filmsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Double-elimination, reseeding and 20 teams: MLS plans potential overhaul of playoffs | MLS | The Guardian
description: The format would resemble that of Australian rules football, and the changes would pair with a structural move from two conferences to five divisions
Author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
Headline: The format would resemble that of Australian rules football, and the changes would pair with a structural move from two conferences to five divisions
Content: The MLS postseason, which culminates in the annual MLS Cup final, will have a new look beginning in 2028.Photograph: Chris Arjoon/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenThe MLS postseason, which culminates in the annual MLS Cup final, will have a new look beginning in 2028.Photograph: Chris Arjoon/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockMLSDouble-elimination, reseeding and 20 teams: MLS plans potential overhaul of playoffsFormat would resemble that of Australian rules footballLeague will ditch conferences for five-division setupExclusive byPablo Iglesias MaurerThu 20 Aug 2026 08.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 12.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMajor League Soccer is planning a significant overhaul of its playoff format, multiple league and club sources told the Guardian this week. The changes, which would debut in 2028 alongside the league’s shift to a fall-to-spring schedule, could include a “double-elimination” component and see as many as 20 teams feature. Sources spoke on the condition of anonymity as they were not authorized to discuss the league’s plans.The Guardian has viewed a potential schedule for the new format, in which the playoffs start in late April and unfold over roughly three weeks withMLSCup being played on Sunday 21 May 2028. The changes to the playoff format would pair with long-reported changes to MLS’s regular season, with the league going to a five-division setup in place of its current Eastern and Western Conference structure.Notably, the 20 potential spots wouldn’t necessarily be evenly distributed among the league’s divisions; instead, all teams would be combined into a single table at season’s end, with the overall 20 best teams advancing to the postseason. Eight of those 20 teams would take part in a play-in round, with four advancing to create a final field of 16 teams.From media deals to roster rules: five priorities for MLS’s new commissionerRead moreThe top eight teams in the combined table would play in a double-elimination round, a move that seems aimed at further incentivizing the league’s regular season matches. A win in that initial round would see a team through directly to the quarter-finals. Teams, sources said, would be re-seeded after each round, ensuring that higher-seeded teams are offered a competitive and hosting advantage throughout the playoffs.MLS says it has yet to make any formal decision on the future of the playoffs.“Major League Soccer is continuing to evaluate potential adjustments to its postseason format as part of a broader review of the league’s shift to a new competition calendar, beginning with the 2027-28 season,” the league said in a statement. “This process remains ongoing, and no determinations have been made at this time.”The proposed format is unique in US sports but closelymirrors that of the AFL,the elite level of Australian rules football. It has used what it calls a “double-chance” format for decades. The league has had discussions with the AFL about its playoff approach, one source said this week.MLS has altered its playoff format many times during its history. In the league’s infancy, eight of its 10 teams qualified for the postseason, which featured a best-of-three format for the conference semi-finals and finals. The format was tweaked again in 2000 and later altered again as teams were added and conferences realigned, moving to two-legged matchups in 2003. In 2019, MLS streamlined things, moving to a single-elimination format.When MLS began its current media rights deal with Apple TV in 2023, the league sought to add more matches to its postseason and introduced its current format, a mishmash of best-of-three and single-elimination matches and also a “play-in” match between the eighth- and ninth-place teams in each conference. That move increased match inventory for television but has been criticized by fans, coaches and players alike.At the time, the league had considered other options, including a “World Cup-style” format which would have seen teams navigate a group stage before advancing to a single-elimination component.MLS is in the midst of regearing itself after this summer’s World Cup. The leaguehas namedLos Angeles FC co-owner Larry Berg as its new commissioner, with Berg set to take the reins from Don Garber next year. Fundamental changes to the league’s roster regulations have been proposed. MLS will play a shortened “sprint season” in 2027 before the most foundational shift in league history: aligning with the international calendar and shifting to a fall-to-spring season.Explore more on these topicsMLSUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Liverpool see £50m bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton  | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Liverpool have had a £50m bid for winger Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton, and are continuing their pursuit of PSG’s Bradley Barcola
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Liverpool have had a £50m bid for winger Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton, and are continuing their pursuit of PSG’s Bradley Barcola
Content: Yankuba Minteh has scored nine goals in 66 games for Brighton since joining the club from Newcastle for £30m two years ago.Photograph: Craig Cowan/ProSports/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenYankuba Minteh has scored nine goals in 66 games for Brighton since joining the club from Newcastle for £30m two years ago.Photograph: Craig Cowan/ProSports/ShutterstockLiverpoolLiverpool see £50m bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by BrightonMinteh targeted as replacement for Mohamed SalahWinger sidelined after recovering from leg surgeryAndy HunterThu 20 Aug 2026 12.59 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 13.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLiverpool have had a £50m bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton. The club are looking to add two wide forwards to Andoni Iraola’s squad before the transfer deadline, with their pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola continuing.Liverpool’s shortlist of targets also includes Minteh but Brighton, who have lost Danny Welbeck to Chelsea and have Kaoru Mitoma out injured, have rebuffed the approach for the 22-year-old winger.Minteh has scored nine goals in 66 Premier League appearances since joining Brighton from Newcastle for £30m two years ago and is reportedly open to becoming a Liverpool player. He is recovering from surgery having suffered a leg injury in a pre-season friendly against Roma this month and could be sidelined for another eight weeks. It remains to be seen whether Liverpool increase their offer for the Gambia international.Liverpool haveadded the versatile Victor Muñozto their forward options this summer for £34.5m but are yet to fill the right-sided void created by Mohamed Salah’s departure. Minteh has mostly operated on the right for Fabian Hürzeler’s team.PSG’s £145m valuation of Barcola has forced Liverpool to consider alternative wide options including the France international’s teammate Ibrahim Mbaye. Interest in Mbaye has not developed into an offer for the 18-year-old at this stage, however.Curtis Jones has been given permission to undergo a medical in Italy after Liverpool agreed a £30m deal with Inter for the midfielder. The Italian champions made a breakthrough in their long-running pursuit of the 25-year-old when offering €30m plus €5m in bonuses on Wednesday.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolTransfer windowBrighton & Hove AlbionnewsShareReuse this content

title: Missing British Athletics coach Leon Baptiste in Marrakech prison | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Leon Baptiste, the British Athletics coach who had not been heard from since visiting Morocco two months ago, is being held in prison in Marrakech, according to the Moroccan Ministry of Justice
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Leon Baptiste, the British Athletics coach who had not been heard from since visiting Morocco two months ago, is being held in prison in Marrakech, according to the Moroccan Ministry of Justice
Content: Leon Baptiste coaches a number of elite athletes.Photograph: John Phillips/Getty Images for Sporting EqualsView image in fullscreenLeon Baptiste coaches a number of elite athletes.Photograph: John Phillips/Getty Images for Sporting EqualsAthleticsMissing British Athletics coach Leon Baptiste in Marrakech prisonCoach had not been heard from for two monthsBaptiste serving a custodial sentence in MoroccoGuardian sportThu 20 Aug 2026 05.27 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 09.52 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLeon Baptiste, the British Athletics coach whohad not been heard from since visiting Moroccotwo months ago, is being held in prison in Marrakech.The 41-year-old, who coaches a number of elite athletes, is believed to have gone to Morocco for the weekend with friends. As of last weekend he had not been heard from since by his athletes or the UKAthleticsofficials who pay him as a Loughborough-based consultant, with messages to his phone not returned.A source from the Moroccan Ministry of Justice said: “According to the information available to the Moroccan authorities, Mr Baptiste did not disappear, nor had he lost contact with his surroundings.“He is currently being held at the local prison in Marrakech, where he is serving a custodial sentence following his conviction by the competent judicial authorities in connection with a misdemeanour case.”A UK Foreign Office spokespersontold the BBC: “We are supporting a British national who is detained in Morocco and are in contact with the authorities.”Explore more on these topicsAthleticsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Max Verstappen signs new Red Bull contract to stay in F1 until 2030 | Max Verstappen | The Guardian
description: Max Verstappen has ended speculation about his future in Formula One by signing a new contract with Red Bull that will extend to the end of 2030
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Max Verstappen has ended speculation about his future in Formula One by signing a new contract with Red Bull that will extend to the end of 2030
Content: Max Verstappen and Red Bull team principal, Laurent Mekies.Photograph: Mark Thompson/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMax Verstappen and Red Bull team principal, Laurent Mekies.Photograph: Mark Thompson/Getty ImagesMax VerstappenMax Verstappen signs new Red Bull contract to stay in F1 until 2030Dutch driver was linked with Mercedes and McLarenVerstappen: ‘I never felt that desire or need to change’Giles Richardsin ZandvoortThu 20 Aug 2026 04.13 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 18.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMax Verstappen has ended speculation about his future in Formula One by signing a new contract with his Red Bull team that will extend to the end of 2030, after almost 18 months of uncertainty around the Dutchman.After being linked with moves to Mercedes and McLaren, Verstappen’s commitment toRed Bullensures that all the major seats in the leading F1 teams are now locked in for next year, just as the sport’s silly season in terms of transfer speculation is beginning.The four-time champion’s future had been a subject of intense debate and not just in reference to switching teams. He had also seriously intimated that he might call time on his F1 career because he was so unhappy with how the new regulations have affected his enjoyment of racing.When discussing the new contract going into his home race this weekend at the Dutch Grand Prix, the 28-year-old said he believed the chances of him leaving F1 had been greater than that of him leaving Red Bull. “I never felt that desire or need also to change [to another team] to try and win somewhere else,” he said in Zandvoort. “If I feel well within the team here, why should I? Because I know that they do everything for me, and they know that I do everything for them once I’m on the track and trying to get the results.”View image in fullscreenMax Verstappen has confidence in Red Bull to return to peak form despite his annoyance with new regulations.Photograph: Márton Mónus/ReutersLooking relaxed and in good humour as he faced the media alongside the team principal, Laurent Mekies, Verstappen expressed his confidence that his team would deliver despite their travails with the new regulations this season. “I think I was closer to retiring than changing team,” he said with a laugh.Verstappen’s previous contract was set to run until the end of 2028 but was understood to include performance-based break clauses, which would have allowed him to leave had he chosen to do so, and while Red Bull have struggled with the 2026 rule set, Mercedes have emerged with a dominant car. Verstappen is sixth in the world championship, 110 points behind the title leader, Mercedes’s Kimi Antonelli.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, had made no secret of his desire to work with Verstappen but with Antonelli having stepped up with extraordinary assurance in only his second season and with his teammate George Russell confirmed, Mercedes were out of the equation. Ferrari similarly locked in Charles Leclerc, while Lewis Hamilton, who has a multi-year deal with the Scuderia and is newly invigorated and successful this season, ensured they too had a set lineup.McLaren then became a potential destination, perhaps as much a negotiating tool for Verstappen’s management with Red Bull as anything else, with a purported switch between McLaren’s Oscar Piastri and Verstappen being floated and the McLaren CEO, Zak Brown, admitting any team would be remiss were they not to consider the possibility of signing Verstappen. However, these rumours were ultimately given short shrift by Brown, who insisted they were happy with their lineup of Lando Norris, the world champion, alongside Piastri.The Dutchman has long said he would like to see out his career with Red Bull, whom he joined as part of their driver programme in 2014, before joining their sister team, Toro Rosso, in 2015 and being promoted to Red Bull early in the 2016 season.While his options for a new team were limited, his dislike for the new regulations and the emphasis they place on energy management was painfully clear, but with F1 and the FIA adapting them already for next year and beyond, and the prospect of the FIA returning to V8 engines with minimal electrical input in 2030, he has been swayed, not least in his faith in his team to turn things round and return further titles.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“First of all, you need to feel good where you’re at. Let’s say, this year, if you are in the fastest car, but you don’t feel well [happy], I don’t think that’s going to last very long,” he said. “So, I feel very good in this team. I have the belief in the people that we can get back to the top. That’s what we are targeting. I still want to win races. I’m hungry to win more.”View image in fullscreenMax Verstappen celebrates winning the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix, his first race as a fullly fledged Red Bull driver.Photograph: Dan Istitene/Getty ImagesFor Mekies, who took over from Christian Horner in July last year, Verstappen is absolutely key in steadying the ship, not least in the driver’s ability to bring the team on as well as wrestling the absolute maximum from the car, as the team principal acknowledged.“What a demonstration of trust Max has put in the team by making this decision,” he said. “We don’t take it lightly; with that trust comes a huge amount of responsibility in living up to being able to give him the best package for the years to come.“The role that Max has in the team, he’s a lot more than the fastest driver in the world for us, he’s the central point of the team.”Explore more on these topicsMax VerstappenRed BullFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 19: Sunderland | Premier League previews 2026-27 | The Guardian
description: Sunderland fans hope Régis Le Bris and his talented squad can continue to surprise the pundits and Opta
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Sunderland fans hope Régis Le Bris and his talented squad can continue to surprise the pundits and Opta
Content: Reinildo celebrates with fans after victory over Chelsea on the last day of the season sealed European qualification. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersSunderland fans hope Régis Le Bris and his talented squad can continue to surprise the pundits and OptaByLouise TaylorThu 20 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 19.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGuardian writers’ predicted position:14th (NB: this is not necessarily Louise Taylor’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)Last season’s position:7thProspectsAfter finishing seventh last season,Sunderlandgo into the new campaign engaged in continental combat for the first time since a brief adventure in the old Cup Winners’ Cup in 1973-74. Will their startling upward trajectory under Régis Le Bris continue or will they succumb to the dreaded second-season syndrome? No one is quite sure.While many like to highlight Sunderland’s relegation-level XG statistics last season, it is important to note that a steadily improving squad lost six players to the Africa Cup of Nations in the winter. Moreover, no key player has been sold this summer, team spirit is superb and pre-season performances have been reassuringly convincing. Le Bris accepts coping with Thursday night football will be a challenge for a club that played in League One as recently as 2022, but insists it is something to be enjoyed rather than feared.It helps that Sunderland still have their captain, Granit Xhaka, controlling midfield. If Xhaka’s decision to recommit to life at the Stadium of Light despite serious interest from Chelsea lifted the pre-season mood, further optimism is provided by the presence of high-calibre individuals, including the fans’ favourite Enzo Le Fée, Chris Rigg, Robin Roefs, Noah Sadiki and Nordi Mukiele, in a versatile squad containing several players comfortable in assorted positions. Brian Brobbey is the sort of robust centre-forward few defenders enjoy marking. “We are growing together,” says Le Bris. “We’ve shown the team is strong.”Graph showing how Sunderland finished in past five seasonsOff-field pictureSunderland are majority-owned by the 29-year-old Swiss-French businessman and trust fund billionaire Kyril Louis-Dreyfus. The son of the late former Marseille owner Robert Louis-Dreyfus has a 64%stake in the club while the remaining 36% is held by the Uruguayan businessman and politician Juan Sartori. The strong relationship between Le Bris and the director of football, Florent Ghisolfi, has helped ensure on-pitch stability, although the past year has brought considerable off-field change, with several key executives replaced as Sunderland’s commercial strategy pivots in a more international direction. While the team toured the United States this summer, other marketing efforts have been concentrated on Africa, with a lucrative, and controversial, front-of-shirt sponsorship with Visit Ghana close to being finalised. More locally, the regeneration of the area adjacent to the Stadium of Light is transforming a post-industrial landscape.Owner-fan relationshipIf Louis-Dreyfus initially attracted a degree of suspicion and scepticism on taking the helm in 2021, he has earned the trust of the fanbase. Supporters were particularly impressed that the owner contacted Xhaka and convinced the Switzerland captain to join from Bayer Leverkusen last summer. Less positively, a creep towards increased corporate hospitality, allied to a divisive new club membership scheme, has polarised season-ticket holders.The managerLe Bris enjoys a spot of close-season surfing on the beaches of his native Brittany, so it is perhaps appropriate that the 50-year-old rode a footballing wave last season. His 2025 Championship playoff winners hit the Premier League ground running and proved they could last the course. Along the way, Le Bris parked his tanks on Newcastle’s front lawn by choreographing two league wins over their rivals. Le Bris holds a doctorate in physiology and biomechanics and a diploma in the mental training of elite athletes. He spent a decade as a highly regarded youth coach at Lorient before taking charge of the first team in 2022, with his love of trigonometry underpinning a coaching philosophy that views football as fundamentally being about triangles.Star signingView image in fullscreenThomas Meunier, who has 83 caps for Belgium, has joined Sunderland on a two-year contract from Lille.Photograph: Jean Catuffe/Getty ImagesSunderland tried and failed to sign Thomas Meunier from Lille a year ago, but patience has been rewarded. At the time of writing, the 34-year-old free transfer is the sole summer signing – quite a contrast to the 14 new faces 12 months ago – but at least two more new recruits are expected before the window closes. Meunier, who has 83 Belgium caps and played at the World Cup, will compete with Mukiele and Trai Hume at right-back. The experience he has acquired throughout a career involving stints at Paris Saint-Germain and Borussia Dortmund should prove useful in the Europa League.Stat attackIf matches were decided by Opta’s expected points metric, Sunderland would have been relegated last season. Instead they are preparing for a Europa League campaign after finishing 11 places higher than the XG figures implied they deserved. It was a wider margin between statistical performance and outcome than any other team in Europe’s big five leagues experienced, for good or bad.How teams finished and their expected position from underlying dataSet for a breakthroughTom Proctor, the son of Sunderland’s first-team coach and former forward, Michael Proctor, is only 17 and starting his second year as an academy scholar.He was included in the first-team squad for the pre-season tour of the United States. Proctor has impressed with his technical ability, awareness and eye for goal. With the squad set to be stretched by Europa League involvement, it will be no surprise if a player who joined Sunderland’s academy at the age of six makes a competitive first-team debut this season.World Cup impactSunderland had 12 players at the World Cup, more than Real Madrid, and such visibility delighted executives charged with growing the club’s commercial revenue streams. Wilson Isidor scored Haiti’s first World Cup goal since 1974 while Brobbey struck three times for the Netherlands. The entire group has since been joined by Meunier, who represented Belgium in the United States.Explore more on these topicsPremier League previews 2026-27SunderlandfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Gianni Infantino eyes junior tournament in Dominican Republic as potential route out of crisis | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: Fifa’s president Gianni Infantino may target meetings around the tournament as a chance to lobby for votes
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Fifa’s president Gianni Infantino may target meetings around the tournament as a chance to lobby for votes
Content: Gianni Infantino is eyeing the tournament as a way of splitting Concacaf votes.Photograph: Luisa González/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino is eyeing the tournament as a way of splitting Concacaf votes.Photograph: Luisa González/ReutersGianni InfantinoGianni Infantino eyes junior tournament in Dominican Republic as potential route out of crisisMeetings around event seen as chance to lobby for votesFifa president may meet his most credible challengerMatt HughesandNick AmesThu 20 Aug 2026 15.03 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGianni Infantino wants to split the European and North American coalition that is seeking to oust him by attending a junior tournament in the Dominican Republic this weekend in another gamble to cling on to power from the Fifa president.The Guardian has learned that Infantino has made plans to attend the U14 Boys Challenge competition organised by the Caribbean Football Union (CFU), 21 of whose associations are voting members ofFifa, despite being urged to stay away from the event by senior figures within Concacaf – the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football – which is working with Uefa to remove him.‘He must resign’: Fans’ petition calls for Infantino to quit as Fifa presidentRead moreInfantino will come face-to-face with the man widely viewed as his most credible challenger, the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, if he follows through with his intention to travel to the Dominican Republic, whose FA invited him to attend before the World Cup sell-off plan emerged last month.The Dominican Republic has since backed the joint Uefa, Concacaf and Asian Football Confederation statement calling for Infantino to hold an independent review of the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, as well as an emergency meeting of the Fifa council.Infantino has largely fallen back on the support of his most steadfast allies by spending time in Morocco and Qatar as the storm has raged over the last month, but is understood to view the CFU meetings as a good opportunity split the Concacaf block and lobby for votes from the region’s smaller nations before next March’s presidential election.Concacaf’s most successful nation, Mexico, is defying the confederation by backing Infantino, who has also received support from two CFU members, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis.View image in fullscreenVictor Montagliani, the Concacaf president, will be at the tournament in the Dominican Republic.Photograph: Omar Vega/Getty ImagesThe Boys Challenge and CFU meetings are not Fifa events, so Infantino’s plan to attend has raised eyebrows. Fifa declined to comment when asked about the president’s movements.Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC are continuing to explore calling for a vote of no confidence in Infantino, which would bring the matter to a head before next year’s election.Under Fifa’s statutes, its council can convene an extraordinary congress at any time if 43 of Fifa’s 211 member associations submit a written request specifying the items they want on the agenda, which can include no-confidence votes.An extraordinary congress must then be convened within three months, although the governing body’s statutes contain no specific provision regarding a vote of no confidence in its president.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionInfantino came under renewed pressure on Thursday with worldwide fans’ groupslaunching a petition calling for his resignation.Fans are being encouraged to sign the petition, which already has support from all six Fifa confederations spanning continental and national fan groups.“The shameful attempt by one individual – the Fifa president himself – to sell off the World Cup to private investors exposed a betrayal football will never forget,” a statement on behalf of the fan organisations said. “Infantino’s plan was stitched together in secret. Negotiated behind closed doors. Hidden from Fifa’s own members and from the millions of people whose passion makes football what it is.“A president who repeatedly betrays football and makes a mockery of our game has lost the right to lead it,” the statement continued. “For the credibility of Fifa – and for the future of the game – he must resign.”Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: European playoffs: Rangers scrape first-leg win as Brighton draw in Norway | European club football | The Guardian
description: Ryan Naderi gave Rangers a 1-0 Conference League playoff first leg win against Jablonec, while Brighton drew 0-0 at Tromsø
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Ryan Naderi gave Rangers a 1-0 Conference League playoff first leg win against Jablonec, while Brighton drew 0-0 at Tromsø
Content: Ryan Naderi’s goal gave Rangers a slender advantage to take to Czechia next week.Photograph: Luke Nickerson/Rangers FC/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRyan Naderi’s goal gave Rangers a slender advantage to take to Czechia next week.Photograph: Luke Nickerson/Rangers FC/ShutterstockEuropean club footballEuropean playoffs: Rangers scrape first-leg win as Brighton draw in Norway10-man Rangers hang on for 1-0 win against JablonecTromsø 0-0 Brighton; Hearts 2-2 Rapid ViennaPA MediaThu 20 Aug 2026 18.54 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 19.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRyan Naderi’s second-half strike gave an unconvincingRangersa narrow 1-0 win in the first leg of theirConference Leagueplayoff tie against Czech sideJablonecat Ibrox. Derek McInnes got his first win as Rangers manager at the fifth time of asking with a 5-1 thumping of St Mirren on Sunday but there was regression in the goalless first half which brought boos at the interval whistle.The Govan side pepped up after the break and Naderi opened the scoring from close range in the 50th minute but in the 78th minute the substitute Cammy Devlin was sent off – minutes after coming off the bench – for a high tackle on Jiri Slama to leaveRangersto see out the game with 10 men.Fabian Hürzeler, admitted: “It’s not the result we hoped for,” afterBrightonwere held to a frustrating goalless draw againstTromsøin Norway. The Seagulls, who open the new domestic campaign against Aston Villa on Sunday, created several good chances but could not find a way past the Tromsø keeper Jakob Haugaard.View image in fullscreenBrighton players applaud the fans after their draw at Tromsø.Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesThe winger Ibrahim Osman – making his Brighton debut after three loan spells away – looked particularly lively during the first half. Tromsø then almost snatched a late winner on the break, but the defender Isak Vadebu sent his shot wide as the tie went into next week’s second leg at the Amex Stadium all square.Hearts’ head coach, Wouter Vrancken, hopes James Wilson’s stunning goal in the 2-2 Conference League draw withRapid Viennais a sign of things to come from the youngster. He drilled in an unstoppable drive from 30 yards just moments after coming on as the hosts took the lead in the playoff first leg.“He’s a young lad so for sure it will be extra special. Let’s hope he can make the next steps,” Vrancken said.Wilson’s effort marked an impressive turnaround after Josh McPade cancelled out Serge-Philippe Raux-Yao’s first-half header. However, Rapid scrambled in a late equaliser through Nikolaus Wumbrand to ensure the tie remains on a knife edge ahead of next week’s return leg.David Gray, theHibernianhead coach, savoured “a massive performance and a massive result” as his side kept themselves on course to reach the main phase with a spirited 0-0 draw in Belgium againstGent.For the second Thursday night in a row, Hibs ground out a stalemate on foreign soil after they eliminated Shkendija in North Macedonia last week. It could have been even better for them if Owen Elding’s 15th-minute penalty had not been saved by Davy Roef.Motherwellmade a whirlwind start at home toFreiburg, with Regan Charles-Cook sidefooting in Emmanuel Longelo’s cutback after just 73 seconds. But Matthias Ginter headed Freiburg level on 27 minutes and netted a second from the spot, after Martin Moormann was shown a straight red card on 65 minutes via a video assistant referee review.The substitute Keisuke Goto added a third with a stoppage-time header to leave the Scottish side with a 3-1 deficit mountain to climb in Germany next Thursday.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Northern Irish champions,Larne, took a big step towards the league phase after a 2-0 win at 10-manLincoln Red Imps.The match looked set to finish goalless in Gibraltar after Red Imps had held firm following Yussef Flalhi’s 29th-minute red card. However, visiting Larne made their pressure pay when Paul O’Neill struck with five minutes left before fellow substitute Kevin O’Hara’s stoppage-time breakaway goal ensured Gary Haveron’s side will have a cushion ahead of the second leg at Inver Park.Shamrockwere held to a 1-1 draw at home by the Finnish sideKuPSafter they conceded an 85th-minute equaliser. The former Sheffield United full-back Enda Stevens put the Irish side ahead after 49 minutes, but they were denied a precious victory when the one-time Charlton youngster Piotr Parzyszek levelled late on at Tallaght Stadium.View image in fullscreenMohamed Salah had a tricky night against Ferencvaros.Photograph: Anadolu/Getty ImagesIn theEuropa League, Mohamed Salah played all 90 minutes of his home debut asTrabzonsporhostedFerencvaros, but the Hungarian side won 1-0 and their Turkish opponents had Chibuike Nwaiwu sent off in added time.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballEuropa LeagueConference LeagueBrighton & Hove AlbionTromsoTrabzonsporFerencvarosnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Enzo is a Chelsea player,’ says Alonso but doesn’t guarantee Fernández’s future | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: Xabi Alonso has refused to offer any guarantee that Chelsea will hold firm if Manchester City try to sign Enzo Fernández
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Xabi Alonso has refused to offer any guarantee that Chelsea will hold firm if Manchester City try to sign Enzo Fernández
Content: Enzo Fernández could still leave Chelsea before the transfer window closes on 1 September.Photograph: Paul Dennis/TGS Photo/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenEnzo Fernández could still leave Chelsea before the transfer window closes on 1 September.Photograph: Paul Dennis/TGS Photo/ShutterstockChelsea‘Enzo is a Chelsea player,’ says Alonso but doesn’t guarantee Fernández’s futureMidfielder linked with £120m move to Manchester CityChelsea still interested in Bournemouth’s Alex ScottJacob SteinbergThu 20 Aug 2026 11.50 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleXabi Alonso has refused to offer any guarantee that Chelsea will hold firm ifManchester Citytry to sign Enzo Fernández.Fernández’s future remains up in the air and the prospect of him leaving Stamford Bridge has not gone away, even thoughChelsea’s unofficial deadlinefor clubs to make written bids of £120m for the 25-year-old Argentina midfielder has already passed. City,who are also tracking Roma’s Manu Koné, have targeted Fernández as part of their midfield rebuild after Rodri’s move to Barcelona and are weighing up whether to make a move before the transfer window shuts.Instant classics, odd inspirations and barcodes: 2026-27’s best and worst kitsRead moreChelsea, who have identified Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton as possible replacements for Fernández, know the situation is fluid. The player has made no secret of his desire to leave the club and Alonso was noncommittal when asked if he would still be part of his squad at the end of the transfer window.“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” the former Real Madrid manager said. “He’s a top player. He’s training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team. Very integrated, and we are happy with him. He’s getting ready for Monday.”Chelsea open their Premier League campaign with a trip to Fulham on Monday night. Fernández is expected to be in the squad but Alonso dodged another question about whether the £106.7m midfielder has told him he wants to stay. “He’s training really well. I see him with a good attitude. That’s what we want. Everyone is trying their best to prepare for the kick off of the Premier League.”Chelsea will want a new midfielder if Fernández goes. They are huge admirers of Scott but have already failed with one offer for the 22-year-old and have been told that Bournemouth will resist a sale this summer. Wharton is an alternative, although City have had an offer for the England midfielder rejected by Palace.Alonso is also looking to trim down his squad before the window shuts. Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu have fallen down the pecking order up front and are likely to leave. Everton, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest are tracking Delap. Chelsea also have interest in Pedro Neto and Malo Gusto while Palace want to bolster their defence by signing Axel Disasi on loan.It has been another busy summer at Chelsea and Alonso must also consider whether keeping Fernández would sit well with supporters. Some booed him during the friendly win over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge last week. “He was not just booed, they as well chanted his name,” Alonso said. “It’s not unusual, it can happen. We support him. We have a great player with Enzo, he’s a top player, he’s been so important.”There was a reminder of Fernández’s standing when he wore the captain’s armband after coming on against Sociedad. Alonso could continue to use him as Reece James’s deputy. “Reece is the first captain and we have other leaders, other personalities that share the same role,” the Spaniard added.Explore more on these topicsChelseaTransfer windowManchester CitynewsShareReuse this content

title: Michael Carrick rejects ‘ridiculous’ talk of easy start to Manchester United season | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that facing promoted Hull and Ipswich constituted a favourable start to the season for Manchester United
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that facing promoted Hull and Ipswich constituted a favourable start to the season for Manchester United
Content: Michael Carrick hopes to bring players in before the transfer window closes.Photograph: Charlotte Tattersall/Manchester United/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick hopes to bring players in before the transfer window closes.Photograph: Charlotte Tattersall/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester UnitedMichael Carrick rejects ‘ridiculous’ talk of easy start to Manchester United seasonUnited face promoted sides Hull and Ipswich‘It’s not favourable. It’s an easy thing to throw out there’Jamie JacksonThu 20 Aug 2026 13.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that Manchester United’s opening two games against Hull and Ipswich represent a favourable start to the season. United travel to Hull for Saturday’s opening match before hosting Ipswich a week on Sunday. Both sides were promoted from the Championship.Carrick is adamant neither game will prove easy. “For all of us to know this league, there’s no favourable start, I think it’s a tough start,” he said. “A promoted team away from home is a tough game.Frugal or foolish? Manchester United may regret not backing CarrickRead more“I’ve been involved in them in the past so I’m fully aware of what’s coming at us on Saturday, what we’ve got to be ready for. So it’s not favourable. It’s an easy thing to throw out there. But it’s pretty ridiculous in a certain way, [we are] not taking it that way at all.”Carrick guided United to third last season after takinginterim charge in January. He becamepermanent manager four months lateron the back of his success in the role. He was asked if leading United to the title this season is a realistic ambition. “It is going to be a jump,” said the 45-year-old. “I would never say we can’t – I don’t believe that. But it’s about what we are capable of doing as a group.“The run of form we had last season gives us a lot of confidence, but we know there is a whole new step to make. We are pushing to do that. It’s exciting. We have the potential to achieve things and we will definitely give it everything we can. We have to believe we are a good team and can do good things.”United are hopeful ofsigning the midfielder Carlos Balebafrom Brighton for less than £75m and remain in the market for a left-back. “We are looking to strengthen the squad, working towards that,” Carrick said. “We are trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it and are in a good way to doing that so far.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMason Mount’s availability for the trip to Hull is in the balance due to a knock.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks off | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Manchester United’s new-look midfield, Ipswich’s ambition is tested and Kevin Keegan tributes at Newcastle
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Manchester United’s new-look midfield, Ipswich’s ambition is tested and Kevin Keegan tributes at Newcastle
Content: Youri Tielemans faces Hull; Marcos Senesi can calm down Spurs; and Alexander Isak will get a hot reception at Newcastle.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenYouri Tielemans faces Hull; Marcos Senesi can calm down Spurs; and Alexander Isak will get a hot reception at Newcastle.Composite: Getty ImagesTen things to look out for this weekendSoccerPremier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks offManchester United’s new-look midfield, Ipswich’s ambition is tested and Kevin Keegan tributes at NewcastleGuardian sportThu 20 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 19.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Nwaneri out of Arsenal pictureWhile Myles Lewis-Skelly lookslikely to remain at the Emirates, the same can’t be said for Ethan Nwaneri. The 19-year-old was outstanding in his breakthrough season for Arsenal in 2024-25 but barely featured last season and was sent on loan to Marseille. That didn’t really work out and Arsenal are now exploring another temporary move to ensure Nwaneri gets regular football this season. Milan, RB Leipzig, Dortmund and Fulham are all thought to be interested, with Nwaneri unlikely to feature on the bench for Friday’s opener against Coventry as a result. Whether Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are available remains to be seen as Arsenal attempt to find suitors for the Brazil duo.Ed AaronsArsenal v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)2New United pair down for Tigers testManchester United’s summer transfer business has focused on recruiting in central midfield. It will be interesting to see who Michael Carrick selects in two key roles for the first game of the season. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been present for more of pre-season than Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute for England at the World Cup and was a late returner to Carrington after a holiday. Carlos Baleba surely will not have arrived in time to start at Hull. Mainoo is in the best position in the long term but if Carrick decides to ease him into the season, it would be intriguing to see how Santos and Tielemans team up, the stress test for a new partnership that could provide the perfect balance of defensive awareness and ability to move the team up the pitch.Will UnwinHull City v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm3Can Ipswich copy Black Cats’ success?Ipswich clearly learned a lot from what Sunderland did a year ago, as they went out and bought a lot of players. The Black Cats quickly moulded their 19 acquisitions into a successful unit but at least they had the positive of a head coach in Régis Le Bris who had his feet under the table. Gary O’Neil is the new man at Portman Road and he has 12 signings – at time of writing – to potentially use for the opener. The record arrival, Emersonn, who has moved to Portman Road from Toulouse, is the most eye-catching of those who have been acquired. The Brazilian has an underwhelming career goalscoring record and a few question marks hanging over his head. Even though it is their first game, Ipswich need to pick up points at home, and to do so require a striker who can cause problems for defenders. How quickly Emersonn adapts will be critical for the Tractor Boys’ success this year.WUIpswich Town v Sunderland, Saturday 3pmView image in fullscreenEmersonn is one of a number of big-money signings made by promoted Ipswich this summer.Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock4Glasner’s tough Diomande ready for debutAugust is the season for debuts and no one will be more satisfied than Oliver Glasner when Ousmane Diomande steps over the white line at the City Ground. Glasner wanted the Ivorian centre-back to replace Marc Guéhi at Crystal Palace, six months before the England defender departed forManchester City. Diomande, a £34m buy from Sporting, is expected to line up in a back three for Nottingham Forest against Leeds, when the Austria midfielder Xaver Schlager, who played for Glasner at Wolfsburg, could also make his Forest bow. Diomande is a quick and physical defender but another aspect of his appeal is his aerial power at set pieces. “They’ve both played Champions League football and they are used to competing for titles,” said Glasner. “They can add this winning mentality.”Ben FisherNottingham Forest v Leeds, Saturday 3pm5Serene Senesi can bring calm to SpursCristian Romero has taken his maverick brand of defending to Atlético Madrid, upsetting neutralPremier Leaguewatchers. His compatriot Marcos Senesi has arrived to shore up things at the back as Roberto De Zerbi desperately tries to steer Spurs away from a third straight season of battling relegation. The all-action Romero had his qualities as a leader and defender but never felt dependable, which is what most want from a centre-back and captain. Senesi impressed during his time at Bournemouth, rarely making headlines but proving himself a calm presence at the back. The Argentinian is good on the ball and will be more adventurous in possession than his countryman. He is yet to be sent off in three seasons as a Premier League player – Romero was dismissed twice in 2025-26 alone, not to mention a one-match ban and a fine for his behaviour towards a referee. His calmness will improve Spurs.WUBrentford v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm6Villa head south besieged by problemsIt is surely not how Unai Emery envisaged the countdown to Aston Villa’s season-opener at Brighton on Sunday – and certainly not as he enjoyed the afterglow from the club’s Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May. The manager has an extraordinary number of problems. Take the midfield where the new signings João Gomes and Johan Manzambi are injury doubts. Note: Amadou Onana is a long-term casualty while Youri Tielemans has been sold. It goes on. Emery is about to lose Ezri Konsa to Arsenal – in a summer where Villa have also sold Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne. They are trying to move on Emi Martínez, while the future of Ollie Watkins is uncertain, with Al-Hilal circling. For the cherry on top, the rampaging 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo is a fitness concern. Emery’s teamsheet will be very interesting. Will he pitch the new goalkeeper, Zion Suzuki, who only signed on Wednesday, straight in?David HytnerBrighton v Aston Villa, Sunday 2pm7Maresca must win to silence City noiseIs Enzo Maresca already under pressure afterManchester City’s 3-0 schooling by Arsenalin the Community Shield? Maybe not, but if the Italian’s new team go down at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, you do not have to be a soothsayer to picture the scrutiny that will follow. Maresca and City are enduring a difficult transfer window, with Rodri’s departure to Barcelona the headline, a dizzying blow that has to be shaken off. The new Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, has faced City six times in the Champions League with Leipzig and Mönchengladbach, and is sure to order his visitors to go for the jugular at the Etihad. City are vulnerable but Maresca can remedy this with a win of any sort. This, after all, is the job many felt he was the obvious choice for.Jamie JacksonManchester City v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pmView image in fullscreenAnything but a win for Manchester City at home to Bournemouth will increase scrutiny on Enzo Maresca.Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA8King Kev remembered at NewcastleKevin Keegan was supposed to have been the guest of honour at St James’ Park on Sunday, but his death from cancer in July means this meeting of two of his old clubs will turn into a tribute toone of English football’s enduring heroes. Keegan’s family will be present to witness an outpouring of love for the former Liverpool and Newcastle forward and (twice) Magpies manager. Once the game kicks off, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak, a St James’ Park old boy whose decision to force a £125m move to Anfield last summer did not go down well on Tyneside. The Sweden striker, making his first return to Newcastle, has much to prove at Liverpool, and now has a new head coach to impress in Andoni Iraola. Newcastle too have a new face in the home dugout, where Matthias Jaissle will occupy the technical area for so long inhabited by Eddie Howe.Louise TaylorNewcastle vLiverpool, Sunday 4.30pm9Former Madrid managers meet in capitalReal Madrid’s two head coaches from last season meet at Craven Cottage, with the focus on Xabi Alonso, rather than Álvaro Arbeloa. TheFulhamman, however, may have more to prove in the Premier League. His managerial career has been less prominent than that of his Basque rival – and he has clearly insisted on snapping up talent from the Bernabéu. Gonzalo García and César Palacios have made the trip over from the Spanish capital with Arbeloa. It shows great faith from the former Liverpool defender but it does put extra pressure on the trio, their fates now permanently intertwined. All three need a positive start to show they merit being in the Premier League. Otherwise, it would be very easily to criticise them individually and collectively.WUFulham v Chelsea, Monday 8pmExplore more on these topicsFootballTen things to look out for this weekendPremier LeagueArsenalManchester UnitedIpswich TownTottenham HotspurManchester CityfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Maracanã to host opening game and final at next year’s Women’s World Cup | Women's World Cup 2027 | The Guardian
description: The schedule for next year’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil has been released with the opening game and final to played at Rio de Janeiro’s Maracanã
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: The schedule for next year’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil has been released with the opening game and final to played at Rio de Janeiro’s Maracanã
Content: The Maracanã hosted the men’s World Cup final in 1950 and 2014.Photograph: Chris Brunskill Ltd/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe Maracanã hosted the men’s World Cup final in 1950 and 2014.Photograph: Chris Brunskill Ltd/Getty ImagesWomen's World Cup 2027Maracanã to host opening game and final at next year’s Women’s World CupStadium has hosted two men’s World Cup finalsArena Itaquera in São Paulo will host 10 matchesTom GarryThu 20 Aug 2026 11.25 EDTLast modified on Thu 20 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro will host the opening game and the final of next year’s Women’s World Cup. The 78,838-capacity stadium, which hosted the finals of the 1950 and 2014 men’s World Cups as well as the finals of the Olympic football competitions in 2016, will be the venue for Brazil’s opening Group A match on 24 June, before staging the final on 25 July.Fifa released the schedule for all 64 matches for the tournament, which features 32 teams. The draw will take place after more of the qualification playoffs have been contested.‘For future generations’: Brazil working hard to ensure successful 2027 Women’s World CupRead moreBrazil will also play group matches at the Arena Itaquera in São Paulo – which will host 10 matches at the finals, more than any other host city – and at the Estádio Nacional in Brasília. Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo have been selected to host the semi‑finals, with the latter also staging the third-fourth playoff. All eight of the stadiums involved in the finals staged matches at the men’s tournament in 2014.Belo Horizonte – the scene of Brazil’s humiliating7-1 semi-final loss to Germany12 years ago – has been chosen to host a quarter-final. The winners of Group A will play in that quarter-final if they progress that far. Fortaleza, Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo will host the three other quarter-finals.Porto Alegre and Recife are also staging matches in the 10th official edition of the Women’s World Cup and the second to include 32 teams, after the expanded tournament, cohosted by Australia and New Zealand, in 2023.Spain won the title for the first timein Sydney after victory over England.View image in fullscreenSpain beat England in the final of the 2023 Women’s World Cup to lift the trophy for the first time.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images“We can’t wait to witness a new chapter of women’s football history unfold when the world’s best players, coaches, fans and local communities take centre stage in Brazil next year,” said Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino. “I already have goosebumps thinking about the incredible passion, colour and energy that Brazilian fans will bring to the tournament.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe former Brazil captain Aline Pellegrino said: “Each host city will add its ​own unique flavour, making ​this a colourful, joyful ​and unforgettable celebration. The ​world’s best players ‌will feel that ​energy from ​the stands and they will give it back on the pitch through moments and performances that will inspire girls and boys around the world.”It is the first time the women’s event has been staged in South America and the Maracanã will join the now-demolished Råsunda Stadium in Solna, Sweden, and the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California, as having hosted World Cup finals for both the men’s and women’s game.Explore more on these topicsWomen's World Cup 2027Women's World CupWomen's footballBrazilnewsShareReuse this content

title: Jordan Cox reflects on missed opportunities despite England’s big lead against Pakistan | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: England had four half-centurions on day two at Headingley but there were a few regrets on their failure to reach three figures
Author: Taha Hashim
Headline: England had four half-centurions on day two at Headingley but there were a few regrets on their failure to reach three figures
Content: Jordan Cox scored 73 in England’s first innings against Pakistan at Headingley.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJordan Cox scored 73 in England’s first innings against Pakistan at Headingley.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesEngland cricket teamJordan Cox reflects on missed opportunities despite England’s big lead against PakistanCox: ‘We were hoping one of us would have kicked on’Sam Curran will miss rest of the summer due to injuryTaha Hashimat HeadingleyThu 20 Aug 2026 17.09 EDTFirst published on Thu 20 Aug 2026 08.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEngland v Pakistan: first Test, day two start delayed by rain – liveRead moreJordan Cox was one of four half-centurions as England maintained control of the first Test against Pakistan – but there were a few regrets as no one reached three figures on day two in Leeds.“We were hoping one of us would have kicked on and instead of make it just a hundred, make it 150, 160, 170,” said Cox, who hit 73 in his first Test innings at No 3. “And then the game looks, not completely different, but it puts us in definitely a better position.”Nonetheless, England look primed to take a series lead. Harry Brook top-scored with 91 as Joe Root and Dan Lawrence hit 66 and 51, respectively, after rain delayed the start of play until 2.45pm. England closed on 366 for eight, extending their first-innings lead to 195.Ali Usman was the one positive on another tough day for Pakistan, with the left-arm spinner claiming five for 92. “Hopefully, the boys can get 50 runs tomorrow,” said Cox. “You never know, we’ve still got Jamie [Smith] at the crease there and Jofra [Archer], who can still give it a good whack. So hopefully 50-odd runs and then get to our work.”For Cox – who edged behind off Usman – there were mixed emotions as he missed out on a first international hundred, a score that would have been a serious statement while he fills in for the absent Jacob Bethell.“I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70, don’t you? Once I got to 50, I got to about 60 quite quickly, and I was thinking, there’s a chance here – just keep being disciplined. I definitely had it in the back of my mind thinking, you know, you’ve worked so hard, don’t give this opportunity up.”Elsewhere, a Test comeback has been put on hold for Sam Curran after the all-rounder was ruled out of the rest of the English summer with a groin injury. Curran is an option England are considering as they figure out life after Ben Stokes.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenSam Curran has not played Test cricket since August 2021.Photograph: Jacob King/PAThe left-armer was not included in the squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan as he was not considered fully fit, but has been namechecked by Marcus North, the men’s national selector, as an option to balance England’s XI. He will undergo surgery on Friday, ruling him out of the third Test against Pakistan, starting on 9 September at Edgbaston, and the white-ball series against Sri Lanka that month.While a regular member of the two limited-overs teams, Curran – who made his debut as a 19-year-old against Pakistan in 2018 – has not played Test cricket since August 2021.Explore more on these topicsEngland cricket teamEngland v Pakistan 2026CricketnewsShareReuse this content
